decisions.decision: Add the provider-issued execution identifier to the closed enumeration of what evidence may retain in release-contract.md section 7, and change nothing else in that section.
decisions.rationale: A session identifier is not credential material: it grants no access, and under --no-session-persistence it is not even a resumable handle. It is the only value that lets a live evidence record be reconciled against the Provider's own record, which is what the live-evidence gate rule demands. The enumeration is closed, so recording the identifier without naming it would be an unannounced widening of the contract, which is the same defect class as quietly weakening it.

decisions.decision: Do not replace the identifier with its digest.
decisions.rationale: The runner projection already writes the verbatim identifier into the checkpoint, so the value reaches canonical state regardless. Hashing it only in evidence would remove the ability to reconcile with the Provider while hiding nothing.

decisions.decision: Restate the prohibition on prompts and raw responses in the same sentence.
decisions.rationale: The amendment must read as a narrowing addition, not as a loosening. Keeping the prohibition adjacent makes a future reader see the boundary in one glance.

risks: A future task could read the new item as permission to record other Provider-side metadata; the wording confines it to an opaque identifier that carries no prompt, no response content and no credential.
